Genetic diagnostics

How do clinicians make a diagnosis of genetic disease?




1 · Deep phenotyping Detailed clinical examination


2 · Integrate the evidence Signs, symptoms, lab values, imaging, set against: anatomy biochemistry genetics physiology


The bottleneck Assembling all the needed information is difficult and time-consuming


The HRA–HPO bridge + MutationTaster streamlines data integration for clinical diagnostics


Wang Q, et al. (2022) Deep phenotyping and whole-exome sequencing improved the diagnostic yield for nuclear pedigrees with neurodevelopmental disorders. Mol Genet Genomic Med. 2022 May;10(5):e1918

title: Genetic diagnostics
text:
IPEX syndrome

What can a published IPEX case report teach us about data-driven diagnosis?


The disease Immune dysregulation, polyendocrinopathy, enteropathy, X-linked syndrome (IPEX)


The defect A prototypic defect in the natural regulatory T cell compartment, leading to immunodeficiency, autoimmunity, enteropathy and colitis


The gene Many IPEX patients have defects in the transcription factor FOXP3, which determines the fate and immunosuppressive activity of natural and some induced regulatory T cells


Source of the clinical data: Baud O, et al. (2001) Treatment of the immune dysregulation, polyendocrinopathy, enteropathy, X-linked syndrome (IPEX) by allogeneic bone marrow transplantation. N Engl J Med 344:1758-62

Family history









Mother Unexplained spontaneous abortion in the fourth month of one pregnancy


Four healthy daughters Aged 11, 16, 18 and 19


One son, died at 4.5 months Intractable diarrhea, thrombocytopenia, insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, ichthyosiform dermatitis. Duodenal biopsy: villous atrophy. Autopsy: lymphocyte and plasmocyte infiltration of liver, small bowel, colon and pancreas


No diagnosis was made at the time

title: MYO5B
text:
MYO5B



Protein family MYO5B is an actin filament-based motor protein that binds select GTPase RAB proteins, including RAB8


Function
Dysfunction of MYO5B leads to lack of microvilli on the surface of enterocytes and occurrence of intracellular vacuolar structures containing microvilli.

title: IBD and IEI
text:
IBD: Rare and common









Common Intestinal infections that nearly everyone gets once in a while


Crohn disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC) Together termed inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), ca. 1:200 individuals


Rare Inborn errors of immunity (IEI), monogenic diseases that can present with IBD-like immunopathology, often severe and early-onset



image: Uhlig HH. Monogenic diseases associated with intestinal inflammation: implications for the understanding of inflammatory bowel disease. Gut. 2013 PMID: 24203055.

title: IBD and IEI
text:
IBD: Pathways









Pathway interaction between key genes associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and IBD-like monogenic disorders


Understanding rare diseases with IBD-like features may provide insight for treating common forms



image: Uhlig HH. Monogenic diseases associated with intestinal inflammation: implications for the understanding of inflammatory bowel disease. Gut. 2013 PMID: 24203055.

title: IBD and IEI
text:
IBD: Pathophysiology









The model Key intestinal defence functions and cellular immune regulation components are impaired in monogenic disorders with an IBD-like phenotype


The defects Epithelial barrier and response, neutrophil numbers, phagocytosis and bacterial killing, and gut innervation. Together they increase bacterial translocation across the epithelium and bacterial survival



image: Uhlig HH. Monogenic diseases associated with intestinal inflammation: implications for the understanding of inflammatory bowel disease. Gut. 2013 PMID: 24203055.

title: IBD and IEI
text:
Rare in common

Is “common disease” always what it seems?


70 of 1480 (4.73%) participants with IBD, from five clinical trials, had pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in a relevant gene


31 of 33 of those with a rare disease-causing variant showed no or only a short-term response to adalimumab, a TNF-α inhibitor approved by the FDA for Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis


In clinical practice, rare forms of common disease may be difficult to recognize. Misdiagnoses of rare diseases as common ones are not infrequent.



Rahimov F, et al. (2025) Common Diseases in Clinical Cohorts - Not Always What They Seem. N Engl J Med 393:1589-1598
Robinson PN (2025) A Rare-in-Common Paradigm for Precision Genomic Medicine. N Engl J Med 393:1648-1649
